name: CMC Markets
description: CMC Markets is a London-headquartered, LSE-listed forex and CFD broker founded in 1989. Regulated by the FCA, ASIC, BaFin, MAS, FMA and CIRO, it offers 12,000+ instruments across its proprietary Next Generation platform, MetaTrader 4, and TradingView. The broker serves retail and professional clients globally with spread betting (UK) and CFD trading accounts.
pros: FCA, ASIC, BaFin, MAS regulated — four Tier-1 licences with FSCS compensation up to GBP 85,000 for UK clients
12,000+ instruments — one of the largest product ranges of any retail CFD broker globally
No minimum deposit — genuinely zero barrier to entry
LSE-listed since 2016 with quarterly financial reporting — full transparency on company health
Proprietary Next Generation platform with advanced charting, pattern recognition, and client sentiment tools
Guaranteed stop-loss orders available — a genuine risk management edge most brokers do not offer
cons: GBP 10/month inactivity fee kicks in after 12 months — catches longer-term position traders off guard
No MetaTrader 5 support — stuck on MT4 if you want MetaTrader
FX Active pricing structure is opaque — $5 per $100k traded is harder to compare than a flat per-lot commission
Card fees of 1% credit / 0.6% debit in Australia and 1.5% in New Zealand — not prominently disclosed
68% retail loss rate — slightly above the industry average for Tier-1 regulated brokers
withdrawal_time: Same-day bank transfer (before 4pm UK), 1-5 days card
warning_note: FCA has issued a clone warning for 'CMC Global Markets' — a fraudulent entity using a similar name to CMC Markets. Verify you are on cmcmarkets.com before depositing. GBP 10/month inactivity fee applies after 12 months of no trading.

comparison_block.heading: CMC Markets vs IG — Which Is Better in 2026?
comparison_block.body: IG edges CMC on raw forex spreads — 0.6 pips average EUR/USD versus CMC's 0.7. But CMC wins on platform depth and instrument count (12,000+ vs IG's 17,000+, though CMC's charting tools are arguably superior). CMC's guaranteed stop-loss orders offer genuine downside protection that IG charges more for. For UK spread bettors, both are legitimate choices. Pure scalpers favour IG's tighter spreads. Traders who value platform tools and want more indices or shares CFDs should lean CMC.

long_review.hot_take: CMC Markets has been around since 1989 and still cannot offer a flat per-lot commission on its FX Active account. The $5 per $100,000 traded structure sounds clever until you realise it makes cost comparison nearly impossible for the average trader. And that is likely the point. When your competitor charges $3.50 per lot and you charge a percentage of notional value, you are banking on traders not doing the maths. The platform is genuinely excellent — but that pricing opacity is a choice, not an accident.

sections.heading: Is CMC Markets Worth Your Money in 2026?
sections.body:
Thirty-five years in operation and a London Stock Exchange listing since 2016 — that is the kind of track record most brokers cannot fake. CMC Markets holds four Tier-1 licences (FCA, ASIC, BaFin, MAS) and publishes quarterly financials like any public company must. The Next Generation platform is genuinely one of the best proprietary platforms in retail trading, with pattern recognition scanning and client sentiment data built in rather than bolted on. Same-day withdrawals via bank transfer are publicly reported as reliable by the majority of users.

The honest catch sits in the fee structure. Standard account spreads of 0.7 pips EUR/USD are fair but not best-in-class — IG offers 0.6 and Pepperstone's Razor comes in at 0.0 plus $7 commission. The FX Active account promises tighter spreads but charges $5 per $100,000 traded, which makes direct cost comparison deliberately difficult. And that GBP 10/month inactivity fee after 12 months will catch anyone who trades seasonally or takes a break.

This broker suits experienced traders who value platform depth and instrument access over rock-bottom pricing. If you trade regularly across multiple asset classes and want Tier-1 regulation without compromise, CMC Markets earns its place on your shortlist for 2026.

sections.heading: Is CMC Markets Regulated? — Licence Check 2026
sections.body:
Yes — and regulated properly, not the offshore-with-a-badge type. CMC Markets UK plc holds FCA licence 173730, verified on the FCA register. The Australian arm (CMC Markets Asia Pacific Pty Ltd) holds ASIC licence 238054. German operations run through BaFin, Singapore through MAS, New Zealand through the FMA, and Canada through CIRO. That is six regulators across four continents, all independently verifiable.

What this means for your money depends on where you live. UK clients get FSCS protection up to GBP 85,000 if CMC Markets fails — real compensation, not just words on a page. EU clients under the German entity qualify for ICF coverage up to EUR 20,000. Australian clients get segregated funds but no compensation scheme — ASIC does not offer one. Same story for Singapore and New Zealand: segregation yes, government-backed insurance no.

Leverage caps follow the expected pattern. FCA and ASIC retail clients get 1:30 on majors, 1:20 on minors, 1:10 on commodities. International entity clients may access up to 1:500 depending on classification. Client funds are held in segregated accounts across all entities — this is a regulatory requirement, not a favour.

The FCA has issued a clone warning for a fraudulent entity called 'CMC Global Markets' that is not connected to the legitimate CMC Markets. Always verify you are accessing cmcmarkets.com directly. NAFT last reviewed CMC Markets regulation in January 2026.

sections.heading: CMC Markets Spreads, Fees and Accounts — What Do You Actually Pay in 2026?
sections.body:
On the Standard CFD account, you pay 0.7 pips average on EUR/USD with zero commission — that is $7.00 all-in per standard lot round-turn (broker-stated). Fair, but not the tightest in the market. IG manages 0.6 pips on the same pair, and Pepperstone Razor delivers 0.0 pips plus $7 commission for roughly the same all-in cost with better raw pricing.

The FX Active account drops spreads to 0.0-0.2 pips but charges $5 per $100,000 notional traded. On a standard lot of EUR/USD at current rates, that works out to roughly $10 round-turn in commission alone — before the spread. Total all-in cost lands around $10-$12 per lot depending on the session. Compare that to IC Markets at $7 flat or Pepperstone at $7 flat and you see why the percentage-based model frustrates traders who actually do the arithmetic.

Spread betting is available for UK clients only — same 0.7 pips, zero commission, with the tax-free wrapper that makes it attractive for UK-resident traders who qualify. Guaranteed stop-loss orders are available across all accounts at a premium — genuinely useful for overnight gap protection.

Hidden costs to watch: GBP 10/month inactivity fee after 12 months of no trades. Credit card deposits cost 1% in Australia and 1.5% in New Zealand. Debit cards incur 0.6% in Australia. UK and EU card deposits are free. No deposit or withdrawal fees for bank transfer globally.

table.footnote: All spread figures are broker-stated averages. Actual spreads vary by session and market conditions. Leverage caps apply to retail clients under FCA/ASIC — professional clients may access higher leverage.

sections.heading: How Fast Can You Get Your Money Out of CMC Markets?
sections.body:
Same-day processing on bank transfer withdrawals submitted before 4pm UK time — that is the headline, and it holds up across publicly reported user experiences. PayPal withdrawals typically clear within 1-2 business days. Card withdrawals (Visa/Mastercard) take 1-5 business days depending on your bank's processing speed, not CMC's.

Deposits are faster still. Open Banking gives UK clients instant funding. Bank transfers arrive same-day if sent early. Card deposits are near-instant. No deposit fees anywhere for UK/EU clients — a genuine zero across the board.

The one catch: first-time withdrawals may trigger additional KYC verification. This is standard practice for FCA-regulated brokers and not a red flag, but it can add 1-2 business days to your first payout. Get your documents verified at account opening and you will avoid this entirely.

table.footnote: Processing times are broker-stated. Card fees of 1% credit / 0.6% debit apply in Australia; 1.5% in New Zealand. UK/EU deposits and withdrawals are fee-free.

sections.heading: CMC Markets Withdrawals in 2026 — The Real Picture
sections.body:
Trustpilot shows a 4.3/5 rating (publicly reported) with withdrawal speed being one of the most commonly praised aspects. The majority of verified reviews confirm same-day or next-day processing for bank transfers. This is consistent with what you would expect from an LSE-listed, FCA-regulated firm — they cannot afford the reputational damage of slow payouts.

The complaint pattern is narrow and specific: first-time withdrawals occasionally face KYC-related delays of 2-5 business days while documents are verified. A small number of users report delays when withdrawing to a different payment method than the one used for deposit — this is standard anti-money-laundering procedure, not obstruction. No credible pattern of large-sum withdrawal refusals exists in public records.

If your withdrawal stalls beyond the stated timeframe: first, check your email for KYC requests you may have missed. Second, contact support via live chat (faster than email) and request a reference number. Third, if unresolved after 5 business days, escalate through the FCA complaints procedure — CMC Markets is required to respond within 8 weeks. For UK clients, the Financial Ombudsman Service is your final escalation. Every broker looks good until you need your money back — CMC Markets passes this test for the overwhelming majority of withdrawals.

sections.heading: CMC Markets Red Flags — What to Know Before You Deposit
sections.body: No major regulatory red flags here — CMC Markets is not on any active warning list from any Tier-1 regulator. The issues are operational rather than existential. The inactivity fee is the most common source of complaints: traders who deposit, trade for a few months, then stop — only to find GBP 10 disappearing monthly after month twelve. The FX Active commission model, while not deceptive, is deliberately structured to resist easy comparison with flat-fee competitors. And the lack of MT5 in 2026 is a genuine gap for traders using Expert Advisors built on the newer platform. NAFT last reviewed CMC Markets in January 2026.

sections.heading: Who Should Use CMC Markets — and Who Should Not
sections.body: The not-for list matters more than the for list here. If your strategy depends on the absolute cheapest execution, CMC Markets will frustrate you — 0.7 pips is not bad, but it is not IC Markets or Pepperstone territory either. If you need MT5 for algorithmic trading, you simply cannot use CMC Markets. And if you trade infrequently — a few positions per quarter at most — that GBP 10/month inactivity fee makes this an expensive place to park an idle account.
not_for: Scalpers chasing sub-$7 all-in costs — Pepperstone Razor or IC Markets Raw will save you money on every trade
MT5 algo traders — CMC does not support MetaTrader 5 at all, only MT4
Infrequent traders — the GBP 10/month inactivity fee after 12 months punishes seasonal or occasional traders
US-based traders — CMC Markets does not accept US clients under any entity
for: Experienced traders wanting 12,000+ instruments across FX, indices, commodities, shares, and treasuries from a single account
UK spread bettors who want tax-free trading with a Tier-1 regulated broker and guaranteed stop-loss orders
Traders in Australia, Singapore, or Canada wanting strong local regulation with segregated funds
Technical analysts who value advanced charting — CMC's Next Generation platform rivals TradingView for depth
Risk-conscious traders who use guaranteed stop-loss orders to cap maximum downside on volatile positions

sections.heading: How to Open a CMC Markets Account — Step by Step
sections.body: The process is straightforward and entirely online. Most traders are verified within 24 hours — sometimes faster if you use automated document verification.

steps.title: Register
steps.detail: Visit cmcmarkets.com and select your country. Fill in the online application — personal details, trading experience declaration, and tax residency. The form takes under 5 minutes. You will choose between CFD, spread betting (UK only), or both.

steps.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
steps.detail: Upload a government-issued ID (passport or driving licence) and one proof of address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months). Automated verification often clears within minutes. Manual review may take up to 24 hours.

steps.title: Fund your account and test a withdrawal
steps.detail: Deposit via bank transfer, card, PayPal, or Open Banking — no minimum deposit required. Place a small trade to activate the account, then request a withdrawal immediately to confirm the process works before committing larger capital.

sections.practical_note: Make a small deposit. Place one trade. Request a withdrawal immediately. If it processes cleanly, scale with confidence.

sections.heading: CMC Markets Final Verdict — Is It Worth It in 2026?
sections.body:
NAFT scores CMC Markets 8.1 out of 10 — a strong result built on genuine regulatory depth (four Tier-1 licences), reliable withdrawal processing (same-day confirmed), and a platform that genuinely competes with the best in retail trading. This is a legitimate broker with 35 years of operating history and the financial transparency that comes with being publicly listed. You are not gambling on whether CMC Markets will exist next year.

The risks are manageable but real. The inactivity fee will cost you GBP 120 per year if you stop trading and forget to close your account. FX Active pricing is harder to compare than it should be. No MT5 means no migration path for traders with existing MT5 infrastructure. And 68% of retail accounts losing money is a reminder that the broker makes money when you trade frequently — not when you trade well.

If you want Tier-1 regulation, a deep instrument range, and advanced charting tools, CMC Markets belongs on your shortlist. If cost-per-trade is your primary decision factor, look at Pepperstone or IC Markets first. NAFT recommends opening a demo account on the Next Generation platform before committing — it is genuinely different from anything else in the market, and you will know within a day whether it suits your workflow.

faq.q: Is CMC Markets legit or a scam?
faq.a: CMC Markets is a legitimate broker founded in 1989 and listed on the London Stock Exchange since 2016 (ticker: CMCX). It holds FCA licence 173730, ASIC licence 238054, and additional licences from BaFin, MAS, FMA, and CIRO. UK clients receive FSCS compensation up to GBP 85,000. CMC Markets is not on any active regulatory warning list. A fraudulent clone called 'CMC Global Markets' exists — always verify you are on cmcmarkets.com.

faq.q: How long does CMC Markets withdrawal take?
faq.a: CMC Markets processes bank transfer withdrawals same-day if submitted before 4pm UK time. PayPal withdrawals take 1-2 business days. Card withdrawals (Visa/Mastercard) take 1-5 business days depending on your bank. First-time withdrawals from CMC Markets may take slightly longer due to mandatory KYC verification — completing identity documents at account opening avoids this delay entirely.

faq.q: What is the minimum deposit for CMC Markets?
faq.a: CMC Markets has no minimum deposit requirement — you can fund your account with any amount. This applies across all account types including Standard CFD, FX Active, and Spread Betting (UK). Deposits via bank transfer, card, PayPal, and Open Banking are all free for UK and EU clients. Australian clients pay 1% on credit card deposits and 0.6% on debit cards.

faq.q: Does CMC Markets charge an inactivity fee?
faq.a: Yes. CMC Markets charges GBP 10 per month after 12 consecutive months of no trading activity. This fee only applies if your account has a positive balance and you have not placed any trades for a full year. If you plan to take an extended break from trading with CMC Markets, either close all positions and withdraw your funds, or place at least one trade within the 12-month window.

faq.q: Is CMC Markets regulated in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. CMC Markets Asia Pacific Pty Ltd holds Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) licence number 238054. Australian clients are subject to 1:30 leverage on major forex pairs under ASIC retail rules. Client funds are held in segregated accounts. Note that ASIC does not offer a compensation scheme — unlike the UK's FSCS, there is no government-backed insurance for CMC Markets Australia clients if the broker fails.

faq.q: What platforms does CMC Markets offer?
faq.a: CMC Markets offers three platforms: its proprietary Next Generation platform (web and mobile), MetaTrader 4, and TradingView integration. The Next Generation platform includes advanced charting with 115+ indicators, pattern recognition scanning, and client sentiment data. CMC Markets does not support MetaTrader 5 — this is a notable gap for traders using MT5-specific Expert Advisors or preferring the newer MetaTrader environment.

faq.q: Can US traders use CMC Markets?
faq.a: No. CMC Markets does not accept clients from the United States under any of its regulated entities. This applies to US citizens, US residents, and US Green Card holders regardless of their current location. Traders based in the US seeking similar Tier-1 regulated alternatives should consider brokers holding NFA/CFTC registration such as OANDA or IG US, both of which operate under US regulatory oversight.

faq.q: How does CMC Markets compare to IG?
faq.a: IG edges CMC Markets on raw forex spreads — 0.6 pips average EUR/USD versus CMC's 0.7. CMC Markets wins on platform depth with its Next Generation tools including pattern recognition and client sentiment overlays. Both are FCA-regulated and LSE-listed. CMC offers guaranteed stop-loss orders at competitive premiums. For UK spread bettors, both are strong choices — pick IG for tighter FX costs, CMC Markets for charting tools and broader instrument access across 12,000+ markets.
